clue.text: Relief: Everyman finally grasped insult

indicators.note: grasped says the relief word holds the next piece inside it, as a hand closes round something

parts.note: a relief is a substitute player or stand-in, a sub

indicators.note: finally picks out the closing letter of the setter's pen-name

explanation.surface: Everyman, relieved at last, finally gets the point of an insult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relief' looks like the definition but is SUB, a stand-in; 'grasped' puts N, the last letter of Everyman, inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To snub someone is to slight or rebuff them, a deliberate insult by coldness.

clue.text: Source of illumination, never-ending standard, the shrink

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held: 'Source of illumination, never-ending standard, the shrink (5,4)'. NOR(M) + TH(E) + STAR gives the answer, but 'Source of illumination' must be both STAR and the definition, with no other defining words; it may be cut short.
annotationWithheld.clue: Source of illumination, never-ending standard, the shrink

clue.text: African country, not the last, then old boy heading North to see Italian city

indicators.note: in a down clue, heading north means reading from the bottom upwards, so the whole string is turned round
not the last says the final letter of the country is dropped

parts.note: Angola is a country in south-west Africa
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: Travel itinerary: an African trip, then a schoolfriend heading north to visit Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading North' turns ANGOLOB, the shortened country plus OB, upwards to read the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bologna is the capital of Emilia-Romagna in northern Italy.

clue.text: Sprinkle powder on and wipe powder off

definitions.meaning: to sprinkle a cake with sugar or a surface with talc is to give it a fine coating
cleaning furniture with a cloth removes the fine grime that settles on it

explanation.surface: A puzzling chore that both adds and removes powder.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb has two opposite senses: you can coat a cake with icing sugar, or clean the shelves with a duster.
explanation.definitionFit: One verb covers both: coating with fine particles and cleaning them away, a contronym.

clue.text: Entertainers like Dereks Jarman and Jacobi?

definitions.text: Entertainers like Dereks Jarman and Jacobi?

parts.words: Entertainers like Dereks Jarman and Jacobi?
parts.note: both men share the initials D and J, so they are jokingly plural examples of people with those initials said out loud

explanation.surface: Performers in the mould of a film director and a stage actor.
explanation.walkthrough: Derek Jarman was an English film director and Derek Jacobi is an English actor; each has the initials D.J., spoken as two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Deejays are disc jockeys, music entertainers whose title is the spelt-out initials D.J.

clue.text: Much gusto I convey? Not I!

definitions.text: Much gusto I convey? Not I!

indicators.note: much of, meaning a large part of, says the answer is most of the following words' letters run together

explanation.surface: A deadpan person denies showing any enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through 'gusto I convey', and the whole clue is its own definition: someone unmoved would deny conveying much gusto.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoic endures without showing emotion, so would never convey great enthusiasm.

clue.text: One who stops you going out at night?

definitions.text: One who stops you going out at night?

parts.words: One who stops you going out at night?
parts.note: going out is read as falling asleep, and the person preventing it is a noisy bedfellow

explanation.surface: A strict parent who keeps a teenager in at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going out' suggests a night on the town; read as dropping off to sleep, the culprit is the partner making a racket.
explanation.definitionFit: A snorer's noise keeps a bedfellow awake, stopping them dropping off at night.

clue.text: Note: US rockers given sanctuary

parts.note: R.E.M. are an American rock band from Georgia
an ark, like Noah's, is a place of refuge

explanation.surface: A memo that an American band has been granted asylum.
explanation.definitionFit: A remark is a comment, something noted or observed, so note is a synonym.

clue.text: Eg water treated: our rates unclear

indicators.note: treated, as water is treated at a plant, says the letters that follow are processed into a new order

explanation.surface: Complaint that the water company's charges for treating supplies are not transparent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treated' goes with water in the surface, but it is the anagram signal for all fifteen letters of OUR RATES UNCLEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Water is a resource supplied by nature rather than manufactured, the standard example of one.

clue.text: Then the boasting worked

indicators.note: worked, as clay is worked, says the letters are kneaded into a new shape

explanation.surface: In the past, the bragging paid off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Then' looks like a time word, but it is the definition in the sense 'so' or 'in that case'.
explanation.definitionFit: Then can mean in that case or consequently, and the phrase means given that fact.

clue.text: Communist angry with card game having bloomer

parts.note: red is the colour and nickname of communists
hot under the collar means angry
poker is a card game

explanation.surface: A furious Marxist makes a blunder during a hand of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a mistake; it is literally a thing that blooms, a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The red hot poker is a garden plant with spikes of fiery flowers, so a bloomer.

clue.text: Faulty odograph — no parking — bad driver

indicators.note: faulty says the remaining letters are broken and must be put back together differently
no says the parking letter is taken away from the device name

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A broken distance-recorder and no parking space make for a terrible motorist.
explanation.walkthrough: An odograph records distance travelled; removing P leaves ODOGRAH, and 'Faulty' rearranges those seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A road hog is a selfish, inconsiderate motorist who hogs the road, an idiom for a bad driver.

clue.text: Innocent idyll — but more like a source of amusement, you say?

indicators.note: you say tells us to listen to the spoken comparative rather than its spelling

parts.words: more like a source of amusement
parts.note: an arcade is a place of amusements, so more arcade-like would be arcadier

explanation.surface: Someone suggests a pure rural paradise sounds more like a funfair.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is a made-up comparative: more like an amusement arcade would be 'arcadier', which said out loud matches the name of the pastoral paradise.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcadia, a region of Greece, is the poetic byword for an unspoilt pastoral paradise of simple innocence.

clue.text: Repaired trustable counters

indicators.note: repaired says the following word is taken apart and put together in a new form

explanation.surface: Dependable shop counters have been fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'counters' looks like shop fittings, but it is a plural noun meaning replies that argue back.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebuttals are arguments made to contradict a claim, which is what counters are in debate.

clue.text: Several offices and a bar

definitions.meaning: a building of many offices is an office ...
a bar of chocolate or soap is also a solid slab or chunk

explanation.surface: An office building with a pub in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a pub, but here it is a solid slab, as a bar of chocolate is a block of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A block is a building divided into units such as offices, and also a solid bar-shaped piece.

clue.text: Hazard? Rubbish: that man had engaged

parts.note: to hazard money is to bet it
rot means rubbish or nonsense
that man had shortens to he'd

explanation.surface: A man warns of danger, dismisses it as rubbish, and has been busy.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe of HE'D is dropped in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Betrothed is an old word for promised in marriage, the same as engaged to wed.

clue.text: Type of approval from monks' boss

definitions.meaning: permission given in advance is called ... approval
the head of a priory, or deputy to an abbot

explanation.surface: A form of sign-off granted by the head of a monastery.
explanation.definitionFit: Prior means earlier, as in approval in advance, and is also the title of a monastic superior.

clue.text: Calm provided among fleet

indicators.note: among puts the conditional word inside the word for speedy

parts.note: fleet as an adjective means fast, pacy
provided that means if

explanation.surface: Tranquillity is assured on board the ships of a navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fleet' reads as a group of ships but here it is an adjective meaning swift, PACY.
explanation.definitionFit: To pacify is to soothe or make peaceful, so calm as a verb is a synonym.

clue.text: When I'm working, you don't see the point of me

definitions.text: When I'm working, you don't see the point of me

parts.words: When I'm working, you don't see the point of me
parts.note: the speaker is a fastening whose sharp end is tucked away under a guard when closed and doing its job

explanation.surface: Something complains that nobody appreciates it while it is busy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see the point of me' sounds like a complaint about being useless; literally, the sharp tip is hidden by the clasp.
explanation.definitionFit: A safety pin's point clicks into a covering clasp when fastened, so in use its point is hidden.

clue.text: Went in to dine: get a move on!

indicators.note: in says the first piece sits inside the word for dining

parts.note: to sup is to eat an evening meal
went, in the sense of relieved oneself, is peed

explanation.surface: Someone who went in for dinner is urged to hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Went' is the slangy sense, urinated; that word goes inside SUP.
explanation.definitionFit: Speed up! is an order to go faster, just as get a move on! urges haste.

clue.text: Is a calf, implausibly, getting spa treatments?

indicators.note: implausibly says the arrangement of the letters before it is not to be believed as it stands

explanation.surface: Surprise at a young cow being pampered at a health spa.
explanation.definitionFit: Facials are beauty treatments for the face, a staple of a spa's menu.

clue.text: Approved some damn odd editorials

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A publisher signed off on some very strange opinion pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Nodding the head signals assent, so to have nodded is to have approved.

clue.text: Certain anorak granting owner undrenched life experience, primarily?

definitions.text: Certain anorak granting owner undrenched life experience, primarily?

indicators.note: primarily says to take the leading letter of each of the seven words before it

parts.words: Certain anorak granting owner undrenched life experience

explanation.surface: A particular waterproof jacket lets its wearer go through life without getting soaked.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters spell the answer, and the whole clue describes it: a rain jacket keeps its owner dry.
explanation.definitionFit: A cagoule is a lightweight hooded waterproof jacket, a type of anorak that keeps the wearer dry.

clue.text: Distress increases on meeting Martian?

parts.note: ups as a verb means raises or increases
ET, the extra-terrestrial, stands for any alien such as a Martian

explanation.surface: Anxiety mounts when someone encounters a creature from Mars.
explanation.definitionFit: To upset someone is to distress or trouble them.

clue.text: About to get fleeced? That's rotten

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about
rooked means swindled or fleeced

explanation.surface: Someone about to be cheated complains it is a rotten trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as 'on the point of', but 'About' alone gives C.
explanation.definitionFit: Crooked means dishonest or corrupt, and rotten carries the same sense of moral corruption.

clue.text: Wastes time and sells dodgy lasagne?

definitions.meaning: persisting with a lost cause is idiomatically beating something already dead
a nod to the 2013 European scandal where beef lasagne was found to contain horsemeat

explanation.surface: A trader both idles and peddles suspect ready meals.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the idiom literally: in 2013 ready meals sold in Britain as beef lasagne were found to contain horsemeat.
explanation.definitionFit: To flog a dead horse is an idiom for wasting effort on something already settled or hopeless.

clue.text: Whoa, accumulated prize money in rollover

indicators.note: a rollover, as in a lottery jackpot rolling over, says the word is turned backwards

parts.note: pots are accumulated stakes or jackpots

explanation.surface: Excitement as a lottery jackpot rolls over to the next draw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rollover' belongs to the lottery picture but it reverses POTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoa! is a command to halt, a horse rider's word for stop.

clue.text: Audibly expressed relief in half of LP

indicators.note: audibly tells us to hear the next phrase spoken, not read its spelling

parts.note: someone relieved sighed

explanation.surface: A listener breathed out halfway through a long-playing record.
explanation.definitionFit: An LP vinyl record has two sides, so each side is half of it.
